clue.text: Smoochy Romeo almost lost his parental inheritance

definitions.note: the male-determining chromosome passed from father to son

indicators.note: a lost person is all at sea, so these letters wander into a new order
almost the whole word Romeo, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: An amorous Romeo, too busy smooching, has squandered the family fortune he was left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ROMEO to ROME; 'lost' then rearranges SMOOCHY plus ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetics: a boy receives this sex chromosome only from his father, so it is literally a paternal inheritance.

clue.text: Dear French present, with cents put by

indicators.note: the cents letter is placed next to the other word

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A dear French gift, bought by saving cents.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign word: the feminine French form for 'dear', as in ma chère.

clue.text: Frisky terrier injured batsman, perhaps

definitions.note: in cricket an injured batter may retire hurt; this is one who retires

indicators.note: a frisky animal leaps about, so these letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A lively dog has hurt a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who leaves the field hurt has 'retired hurt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one who withdraws, as a batsman leaving the crease after injury.

clue.text: Ever-changing Alabama city

definitions.meaning: a port on the Gulf coast of the US state of Alabama

explanation.surface: A city in Alabama described as always changing.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means changeable or movable; it is also the name of a southern US port city.

clue.text: Small cat in pain, having a paunch

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
achy means aching, in pain

explanation.surface: A little cat suffering with a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective from the noun for belly: pot-bellied, having a big paunch.

clue.text: Takes up residence in Nov, semi having been given makeover

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone moves into a semi-detached house in November after its refurbishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to occupy a new home, settling into residence there.

clue.text: NCO announced conductor's musical interval

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the sound gives the entry

parts.note: Sir Malcolm Sargent was a famous British conductor
a major third or sixth is a musical interval

explanation.surface: An army NCO announces the conductor's interval at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Malcolm Sargent was a famous British conductor, founder figure of the Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer of senior rank in the army.

clue.text: Short priest cut humorous poem

indicators.note: cut short, the last letter of the churchman's word dropped

parts.note: a cleric is a priest or clergyman
to hew is to chop or cut

explanation.surface: A brief comic poem made by trimming a little priest's words.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-line comic verse about a famous person, named after E. Clerihew Bentley.

clue.text: Playing Scrabble with date — that's given new double chance of success

indicators.note: the extra letter is given a place within the jumble
playing with the letters jumbles them, as with Scrabble tiles

explanation.surface: Playing Scrabble on a date doubles your prospects of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRABBLE and DATE are rearranged, and N is slotted in.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: using two safeguards at once, so success is doubly assured.

clue.text: It's upright to vote right instead of left?

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another, the right taking the left's slot

parts.note: to vote is to elect

explanation.surface: A political quip: is swinging your vote from left to right the upstanding thing to do?
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L in ELECT for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something standing straight and vertical is erect.

clue.text: Curiously lovable wife very absorbed in that part of locomotive

indicators.note: the two letters are soaked up inside the rearranged word
done curiously, oddly, so the letters of lovable are rearranged

parts.note: W is the genealogical abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An endearing wife is deeply engrossed in some piece of a steam engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curiously' turns LOVABLE into BLOALVE; 'absorbed in' places W and V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam engine fitting: the valve used to blow off steam, a component of a locomotive.

clue.text: Irregular soldier sounds like big thug

indicators.note: the phrase announces that a spoken word gives the entry

parts.note: a gorilla is slang for a big brutish heavy

explanation.surface: A rough-looking irregular fighter is described as looking like a hulking brute.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan fighting outside a regular army is a guerrilla; the word means 'little war' in Spanish.

clue.text: Silly argument about recipe for fish

indicators.note: the quarrel goes round the other letter

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
R, from Latin recipe, heads prescriptions

explanation.surface: A daft row in the kitchen over how to cook the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small herring-like sea fish of the north Atlantic.

clue.text: Genre of theatre there's no reason to see?

definitions.text: Genre of theatre there's no reason to see?

parts.words: Genre of theatre there's no reason to see?
parts.note: it also reads as something senseless, beyond reason

explanation.surface: A grumble about a style of drama not worth watching.
explanation.definitionFit: The Theatre of the Absurd is the dramatic genre; its name means contrary to reason.

clue.text: Blows in the main spot we hear turn south

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to spot is to see
to wind is to turn, as a crank

explanation.surface: Talk of punches landing mostly, and turning south.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is the open sea; winds blowing off it are sea winds.

clue.text: Features needed for good health?

parts.note: features are parts of the face, two chins; a toast is drunk for good health

explanation.surface: Which facial features does one need to be in good health?
explanation.definitionFit: A dated drinking toast wishing health, which also reads as a pair of jaw features.

clue.text: Wearing flimsy garments with middle cut out? They're all the rage!

parts.note: wearing clothes is being in them
flimsy means thin

indicators.note: the inner letters are removed, leaving only the ends

explanation.surface: Skimpy clothes with cut-out midriffs are the height of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable items of the moment, the trendy, popular stuff everyone wants.

clue.text: A politician visiting Herts town is going on a walking tour

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so these letters enter the town name

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, an English county north of London
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP calling on a Hertfordshire town is setting out on a hike.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramping means hiking or travelling on foot over a distance, as on a walking tour.

clue.text: Paragon's forlorn hope coming to nothing

indicators.note: forlorn, wretched and lost, signals the letters are scrambled

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A paragon's last hope comes to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a person of unique excellence, like the one mythical bird.

clue.text: Will's fairy trap

definitions.meaning: one of Titania's fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A fairy in a play that is also a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare named a fairy after the gossamer spider's web, which is a trap for insects.

clue.text: Instrument found in old vehicle in America

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is discovered inside an old car in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: A duke needs that woman's love ultimately to remain faithful

parts.note: her means belonging to that woman

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter is used

explanation.surface: A duke needs his lady's love in the end to stay loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere to a cause or belief is to stick with it loyally.

clue.text: In Spain friend regularly warms in glow

indicators.note: every second letter is taken, at a regular interval

explanation.surface: A Spanish friend warms to a glowing fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th... letters of 'warms in glow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for a pal or companion, also used loosely in English.

clue.text: Shrub in hotel garden designed around yard area

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: the letters are laid out anew around one another, as a garden is designed

explanation.surface: A flowering bush grows in a landscaped hotel garden, a yard or so across.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flowering shrub with large globular heads of blue, pink or white flowers.

clue.text: Actor loses money in bet

indicators.note: the letter is lost, taken out of the word

parts.note: a gamble is a bet

explanation.surface: An actor drops his cash in a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable, the Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind, was a film actor.

clue.text: Decree artillery is to surround island

indicators.note: the big guns go round the single letter

parts.note: ordnance means mounted guns, artillery

explanation.surface: A military order sends the artillery to ring an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an authoritative order, especially a local bylaw, is an ordinance.

clue.text: Central parts of rain-cloud on top of Everest inspire

indicators.note: only the inner part of the rain-cloud word is kept, its two ends removed

parts.note: a nimbus is a rain-bearing cloud

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, its summit here

explanation.surface: Climbing scene: rain clouds gathered above Everest's summit, an inspiring sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to fill or permeate with a quality, as to inspire with a feeling.

clue.text: Angry judge, taken in by divorced spouse, reptilian journalist

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
an asp is a snake, a reptile

indicators.note: the judge's word is held inside the journalist's

parts.note: ED, short for editor
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: An irate judge is fooled by a snake-like journalist who used to be married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divorced spouse' looks like the definition's company, but 'Angry' alone defines; ED is the standard crossword editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone thoroughly irritated and fed up is angry.
